anchors.title: MONA — Museum of Old and New Art
anchors.description: David Walsh's subterranean private museum, built into a sandstone cliff on the Derwent River. Catch the camo-painted MONA ROMA ferry from Brooke Street Pier for the proper arrival. The most-visited tourist attraction in Tasmania.

anchors.title: Mt Wellington / kunanyi Summit Drive
anchors.description: 21km drive from the city centre to a 1,271m summit with panoramic views over Hobart, the Derwent and Storm Bay. The summit boardwalk is wheelchair-accessible. Pack a jacket — it's 10°C colder than town.

anchors.title: Battery Point & Kelly's Steps
anchors.description: Wander Hobart's oldest residential neighbourhood — a tight grid of 19th-century cottages, lanes and rose gardens. Descend the convict-built Kelly's Steps to Salamanca and the waterfront.

anchors.title: Cascade Brewery Tour
anchors.description: Australia's oldest continuously-operating brewery, established 1824. 90-minute tour of the heritage stone buildings followed by tastings of Cascade Premium Light and the brewery's seasonal range.

anchors.title: Tasmanian Museum & Art Gallery (TMAG)
anchors.description: Free entry to Tasmania's state museum — natural history, colonial paintings, and exceptional Aboriginal Tasmanian collections in heritage waterfront buildings near Constitution Dock.

anchors.title: Hobart Waterfront Seafood
anchors.description: Eat fish-and-chips from the floating punts at Constitution Dock, then wander the heritage warehouses of Hunter Street and the Henry Jones Art Hotel for waterfront dining.

SATURDAY.title: Salamanca Market
SATURDAY.description: Tasmania's most famous market — 300 stalls under the heritage sandstone warehouses every Saturday 8:30am-3pm. Tasmanian produce, hand-crafted whisky, woollen knitwear, leatherwork and street food.

SUNDAY.title: Farm Gate Market
SUNDAY.description: Hobart's farmers-only market every Sunday morning on Bathurst Street. 50+ Tasmanian producers — no resellers, no imports. 8:30am-1pm.
